summary: A stacked bar chart with a headline total, built for counts that split into parts, such as agent runs that shipped, needed review or failed. Hovering a bar shows its total and the value of each part. A switch moves between ranges like Week and Month, and the bars redraw one after another.
use: When you want to show how many agent runs happened and how they turned out.
When each bar is a total made of a few outcomes or categories.
When the same chart needs a couple of time ranges without a date picker.
features: Stacks one value per entry in `series` in each bar, from the bottom up, coloured from the chart palette or each series' `color`.
The headline number counts up to the total of every bar in the range on screen.
Hovering a bar shows its total with `unit`, followed by each part named by its `tipLabel` or lower-cased label.
With more than one entry in `ranges`, a segmented switch picks the range and the bars regrow left to right.
A legend under the chart names each series, and `format` controls how numbers read.
a11y: The range switch is a role="group" labelled "Range", and its buttons use aria-pressed.
The count-up of the headline total finishes at once when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.q: How do I change the wording in the hover readout?
faq.a: Set `tipLabel` on a series, like "reviewed" for "Needed review". Without it, the readout uses the series label in lower case, and `unit` follows the bar's total.

faq.q: Can I use it for a single, non-stacked series?
faq.a: Yes. Pass one entry in `series` and one value per bar. Each bar is then a single block.

faq.q: How do I hide the range switch?
faq.a: Pass a single entry in `ranges`. The switch only appears when there is more than one.

faq.q: Do the ranges need the same number of bars?
faq.a: No. The chart makes room for the longest range, and bars a range does not have stay empty.
